ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts package#

Cost-tagged facts used by consequence rules.

Importing this package populates REGISTRY through register_fact decorators.

FactContext remains in consequence.context beside AnnotatorContext because the two types differ by lifetime rather than by responsibility.

Submodules#

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base module#

Lazy, memoised, cost-tagged facts for consequence annotation.

Facts form a dependency graph and are computed at most once per FactContext. Declared costs allow strategies to order work and measure avoided computation.

Registered functions have two forms:

  • Boolean facts have public names and may appear in catalogue formulas.

  • Internal value facts have private names and share non-Boolean intermediate values between facts.

Internal value facts must not declare requires because a failed guard returns False. Keep single-use calculations as plain helpers; registration only benefits values shared by multiple facts.

class ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.Fact(*, name, cost, compute, unguarded_compute=<factory>, deps=(), requires=(), documentation='')[source]#

Bases: object

Represent a named, cost-tagged property derived from a context.

deps names values the implementation reads. requires names Boolean preconditions; these are also dependencies and allow evaluation to return False before running the fact.

Variables:

  • name (str) – Registry key and rule atom name.

  • cost (int) – Marginal evaluation cost, excluding dependencies.

  • compute (Callable[[FactContext[Any]], object]) – Guarded computation called by get_fact.

  • unguarded_compute (Callable[[FactContext[Any]], object]) – Original computation used to validate requires declarations.

  • deps (tuple[str, ...]) – Facts read by the computation.

  • requires (tuple[str, ...]) – Boolean preconditions that gate the computation.

  • documentation (str) – Description copied from the registered function.

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.apply_fact_cost_overrides(overrides)[source]#

Override REGISTRY entries’ cost in place from a measured fact-cost table.

Declared cost tiers are untouched for any fact not present in overrides. Also closure_cost’s memoisation cache is cleared so subsequent calls reflect the new costs rather than a stale value computed before the override was applied.

Parameters:

overrides (Mapping[str, int]) – Fact name -> cost unit, typically loaded from annotators/consequence/data/fact_costs.json.

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.apply_packaged_fact_cost_overrides()[source]#

Apply the packaged measured-cost table, if the package ships one.

Call after every fact submodule has registered, since REGISTRY is empty before that. Costs change evaluation order only, never the terms emitted.

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.atom_names()[source]#

Return the Boolean facts a rule may reference.

Returns:

Sorted names of every registered fact that does not start with _.

Return type:

list[str]

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.build_requires_guard(compute, requires)[source]#

Wrap Fact.compute so it short-circuits to False when any required atom is False.

Parameters:

  • compute (Callable[[FactContext[Any]], object]) – The fact’s raw computation.

  • requires (tuple[str, ...]) – Atoms that must all be true for compute to run.

Returns:

compute itself when requires is empty,

else a guarded wrapper around it.

Return type:

Callable[[FactContext[Any]], object]

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.closure_cost(name)[source]#

Return the cost of a fact and its dependencies.

Parameters:

name (str) – The name of a registered fact.

Returns:

The total cost of computing name and every fact it (transitively) depends on,

counting each shared dependency once.

Return type:

int

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.get_fact(fact_context, name)[source]#

Fetch a fact’s value for this context, computing it at most once.

The hottest function in the system, so it does the least it can when tracing is off: one is not None check, shared by both paths, whose body is a single dict bump. Everything else a derivation trace shows – origins, costs, forced-False facts – is reconstructed afterwards from the memo table (ensembl.vep.trace.reconstruct), because it can be. The read count is the one thing that cannot: a replay sees only memo hits, so it never observes the original read pattern. Making the counter unconditional to drop the branch measures 1.30x here.

Parameters:

  • fact_context (FactContext) – The per-overlap memoisation context to read from and populate.

  • name (str) – The name of a registered fact.

Returns:

The fact’s value, from the memo table if already computed.

Return type:

object

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.implied_false(known)[source]#

Extend known facts that are implied False by the current assignment.

The result also explains itself later: a name this added is False here and absent from the memo, which is how trace.reconstruct.forced_false_events recovers the forced-False set and its cause without this function recording anything, and without the explanation duplicating the propagation.

Parameters:

known (Mapping[str, bool]) – A partial assignment of fact names to boolean values.

Returns:

known extended with every fact that requires proves False given

the input, iterated to a fixed point.

Return type:

dict[str, bool]

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.load_fact_cost_overrides_from_package()[source]#

Read the checked-in measured fact-cost table, if any, without applying it.

Returns:

The {fact_name: cost_units} table from ``annotators/data/

fact_costs.json``, or an empty dict if that resource does not exist.

Return type:

dict[str, int]

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.register_fact(cost, deps=(), requires=())[source]#

Register a function as a named Fact in REGISTRY.

requires names are folded into deps automatically because an atom that has to be true first necessarily has to be computed first, so declaring it twice was only ever an opportunity to declare it inconsistently.

Parameters:

  • cost (int) – The fact’s marginal cost.

  • deps (tuple[str, ...], default: ()) – Names of facts that must be computed before this one.

  • requires (tuple[str, ...], default: ()) – Atoms this fact is gated on.

Returns:

A

decorator that registers the wrapped function and returns the original function unchanged, so a module-level reference to it still calls the unguarded body.

Return type:

Callable[[Callable[[FactContext[Any]], object]], Callable[[FactContext[Any]], object]]

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.total_cost(names)[source]#

Return the cost of facts and their shared dependencies.

Parameters:

names (Iterable[str]) – Names of registered facts.

Returns:

The total cost, with every shared dependency (transitively) counted exactly once.

Return type:

int

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.base.verify_requires(fact_contexts)[source]#

Check every requires claim against real contexts.

A wrong declaration would silently produce wrong consequences. This is a sanity check to make sure that never happens.

Checks a fact by running a fact’s compute function without its requires guard, and then checking when the result is True all of its required atoms are True. if one required atom is False, the claim is false and the fact’s compute function is mis-declared.

Running the unguarded body is the whole point: a guarded call can never disprove its own guard, since the guard returns False whenever a required atom is False. Checking through get_fact would therefore pass for every declaration, correct or not.

A body that raises when its required atoms are false is reported too. That is the same class of defect seen from the other side: the body is relying on the guard having already short-circuited, rather than being independently consistent with what it declares.

Parameters:

fact_contexts (Iterable[FactContext[Any]]) – Contexts to check the claims against. Each is reset before use.

Returns:

A description of every requires claim found to be false, or an empty list

if every claim held.

Return type:

list[str]

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.costs module#

Measure fact evaluation costs.

Declared tiers provide relative ordering rather than wall-clock timings. Profiling measures each fact’s self-time and normalises it to the BOUNDS = 1 scale used by declared costs.

Profiling temporarily replaces registered compute functions with timing wrappers and therefore belongs only in explicit measurement runs.

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.costs.declared_vs_measured(measured_self_nanoseconds)[source]#

Return one row per fact comparing its declared tier against what was measured.

Returns:

``(fact name, declared tier label, measured ns, measured

cost in BOUNDS units)``, ordered by declared cost then name.

Return type:

list[tuple[str, str, float, int]]

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.costs.fact_costs_path()[source]#

Return the filesystem path of the packaged measured-cost table.

Resolved the same way load_fact_cost_overrides_from_package reads it, so --write and the loader can no longer disagree about where the table lives.

Return type:

Path

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.costs.normalised_cost_table(measured_self_nanoseconds)[source]#

Normalise every fact’s measured self-time to BOUNDS = 1 and write it to output_path.

The inverse of apply_fact_cost_overrides: BOUNDS = 1 is the same normalisation the declared tier constants use, so a measured table is interchangeable with the declared ones.

Parameters:

measured_self_nanoseconds (dict[str, float]) – Fact name -> mean self-time in nanoseconds.

Returns:

Fact name -> cost in BOUNDS units.

Return type:

dict[str, int]

Raises:

RuntimeError – If no BOUNDS-tier fact was measured, leaving nothing to normalise against.

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.costs.profile_self_nanoseconds(fact_contexts)[source]#

Profile every registered fact’s mean self-time, in nanoseconds, over fact_contexts.

Temporarily wraps every Fact in REGISTRY with a timing shim (restored in a finally block, so a failure partway through still leaves the registry as it found it), then computes every fact for every context.

Parameters:

fact_contexts (list[FactContext]) – Contexts to compute every fact over. Each is reset first.

Returns:

Fact name -> mean self-time in nanoseconds, over every context in which

that fact was computed (every fact is computed for every context here, so the divisor is len(fact_contexts) for all of them).

Return type:

dict[str, float]

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.costs.write_cost_table(cost_table, output_path=None)[source]#

Write a measured cost table as JSON, and return where it was written.

Parameters:

  • cost_table (dict[str, int]) – Fact name -> cost in BOUNDS units.

  • output_path (Path | None, default: None) – Where to write, or None for the packaged table.

Returns:

The path written to.

Return type:

Path

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.helper.intron_offsets_to_genomic_span(intron, strand, low, high, from_donor)[source]#

Return the genomic span of transcript-relative intron offsets.

As usual the genomic span is ascending.

Offsets are 1-based, transcript sense, measured from the intron’s 5’ end (donor) when from_donor is True, else from its 3’ end (acceptor). The donor is intron.start on the forward strand and intron.end on the reverse strand (the intron’s 5’ end in transcript sense is the high genomic coordinate there). Positions are clipped to the start and end of the intron so that they are never outside an intron.

Return type:

tuple[int, int]

Return whether a deletion removes whole codons while preserving a window edge.

VEP’s own test for an inframe deletion (VariationEffect::inframe_deletion): see _matches_codon_edge for its two branches.

Return type:

bool

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.alt_peptide_is_ter(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether the alternate peptide is exactly one stop codon.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.alt_peptide_matches_ref_edge(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether the alternate peptide preserves a reference-window edge.

VEP’s test for an inframe insertion (VariationEffect::inframe_insertion), which it makes on the peptides rather than the codons: residues added at one end of the window leave the reference residues intact at the other. The alternate window is cut at its first stop first, so that an insertion which also introduces a stop is judged on what precedes it.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.cds_length_change_inframe(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether the coding-length change is in frame.

False when the variant does not overlap the CDS. There is then no coding length change to be in frame, and reporting True would contradict this fact’s own requires.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.cds_start_lost(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether the alternate CDS loses the start codon.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.cds_start_retained(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether the alternate CDS retains the initiator methionine.

Computed from the peptides directly rather than as not cds_start_lost. Negating a guarded fact is unsound: when a required atom is false, cds_start_lost short-circuits to False, and not False claims the start codon is retained for a variant that never touches it – which is exactly what verify_requires catches by running this body unguarded. Deriving it here also returns False (not True) when the peptides are unavailable, matching cds_stop_retained. Caching is unaffected: _full_cds_peptide_alleles is the memoised dep both facts read.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.cds_stop_gain(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether the alternate CDS introduces a premature stop codon.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.cds_stop_lost(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether the alternate CDS loses the stop codon.

Requires the alternate peptide to match the reference up to (but not including) the reference’s own stop position, so a frameshift several codons upstream that happens to remove the stop incidentally doesn’t get conflated with an edit that actually changes the stop codon itself.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.cds_stop_retained(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether the alternate CDS retains the stop codon.

Requires stop at the exact same reading-frame position, with the same prefix leading up to it.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.insertion_after_start(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether an insertion occurs after and preserves the start codon.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.insertion_before_start(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether an insertion occurs before and preserves the start codon.

Because variant overlaps start codon (verified by overlap_start_codon fact requirement) the reference peptide should include the start peptide. If the alternate peptide window ends with the reference peptide then it also include the start codon with inserted amino acids before it.

An empty reference peptide is excluded because str.endswith("") is trivially True for any string, which would make this fact vacuously True for every overlap.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.peptide_changed(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether the reference and alternate peptide windows differ.

Return type:

bool

ensembl.vep.annotators.consequence.facts.sequence.peptide_has_X(fact_context)[source]#

Return whether either peptide window contains an ambiguous residue.

“X” comes from an unresolvable codon (incomplete, or an ambiguity code).

Return type:

bool
